'''Adrian Michael Berry, 4th Viscount Camrose''' (15 June 1937 – 19 April 2016)<ref name="Telegraphobit">
{{cite web | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2016/04/19/viscount-camrose--obituary/
|title= Viscount Camrose |accessdate=19 April 2016}}</ref> was a British [[hereditary peer]] and journalist

==Early life and education==
Berry was born in 1937, the elder son of [[Michael Berry, Baron Hartwell|Michael Berry]], who was created Lord Hartwell in 1968 and who disclaimed the family title of [[Viscount Camrose]] in 1995, by his marriage to Lady [[Pamela Smith]], younger daughter of [[F. E. Smith, 1st Earl of Birkenhead]].<ref name="Telegraphobit"/>  He was educated at [[Eton College|Eton]] and [[Christ Church, Oxford]].{{cn|date=September 2026}}

==Career==
From 1977 until 1996, Camrose was the science correspondent of ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''. On stepping down from that position he became the paper's Consulting Editor (Science).<ref name="Telegraphobit"/> 

He was a [[FRGS#Fellowship|Fellow of the Royal Geographical Society]], a [[Royal Astronomical Society#Fellows|Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society]], and a [[British Interplanetary Society|Fellow of the British Interplanetary Society]].

===Climate change===
In his article published in ''[[The Sunday Telegraph]]'' in 2015, Berry denied the [[scientific consensus on climate change]] by claiming that [[climate change]] "has more to do with the violent outbursts of energy that our solar system meets on its eternal passage through the Milky Way" than with carbon dioxide.<ref name="climate_change_2015">{{citation |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/science/space/nightsky/11356838/The-Night-Sky-February-2015-is-climate-change-caused-by-astronomical-events-beyond-our-control.html |work=The Sunday Telegraph |title=The Night Sky February 2015: Is climate change caused by astronomical events beyond our control? |date=1 February 2015 |accessdate=1 February 2016 }}</ref> Berry served on the advisory committee of the [[Global Warming Policy Foundation]], a [[think tank]] that promotes [[Climate change denial|climate-change denial]]<ref name="IJ denial">{{citation|first=Ian |last=Johnston |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/environment/climate-change/nigel-lawsons-climatechange-denial-charity-intimidated-environmental-expert-9350069.html |title=Nigel Lawson's climate-change denial charity 'intimidated' environmental expert |work=The Independent |date=11 May 2014 |accessdate=1 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140511082724/http://www.independent.co.uk/environment/climate-change/nigel-lawsons-climatechange-denial-charity-intimidated-environmental-expert-9350069.html |archivedate=11 May 2014 }}</ref> and claims that policies proposed by governments to [[Climate change mitigation|mitigate]] [[human impact on the environment|anthropogenic]] [[global warming]] are "extremely damaging and harmful".<ref name=bbcnews>{{cite news | url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/8398103.stm | title=Ed Miliband clashes with Lord Lawson on global warming | date=6 December 2009 | work=[[BBC News]] | publisher=[[news.bbc.co.uk]] | accessdate=22 December 2009 }}</ref>

==Marriage and family==
On 4 January 1967,<ref>{{cite news |title=Miss Sulzberger Becomes Bride Of Adrian Berry; Daughter of Columnist Wed in Paris to Son of London Publisher |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1967/01/05/archives/miss-sulzberger-becomes-bride-of-adrian-berry-daughter-of-columnist.html |access-date=6 July 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=5 January 1967}}</ref> Berry married Marina Beatrice Sulzberger, daughter of [[Cyrus Leo Sulzberger II]] (whose family owns ''[[The New York Times]]'') and Marina Tatiana Ladas. The couple had two children:

* [[The Honourable|Hon]] Jessica Margaret Berry (born 11 February 1968)
* [[Jonathan Berry, 5th Viscount Camrose|Jonathan William Berry, 5th Viscount Camrose]] (born 26 February 1970)

==Publications==
*''The next ten thousand years: a vision of man's future in the universes'' (London: Cape, 1974), {{ISBN|0-340-19924-5}}
*''The iron sun: crossing the universe through black holes'' (London: Cape, 1977), {{ISBN|0-340-23231-5}}
*''From apes to astronauts'' (London: Daily Telegraph, 1980), {{ISBN|0-901684-60-0}}
*''High skies and yellow rain'' (London: Daily Telegraph, 1983)
*''The super-intelligent machine: an electronic odyssey'' (London: Cape, 1983), {{ISBN|0-224-01967-8}}
*''The Next 500 Years'' (London: Headline, 1995), {{ISBN|0-7472-4395-6}}
*''Ice With Your Evolution'' (1986), {{ISBN|0-245-54394-5}}
*''Galileo and the dolphins: amazing but true stories from science'' (London: B.T. Batsford, 1996), {{ISBN|0-7134-8067-X}}
*''The giant leap: mankind heads for the stars'' (London: Headline, 1999; rev. edn, London: Headline, 2000), {{ISBN|0-7472-1977-X}}
